assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing to receptor-based therapies, has produced a new drug class that reshapes treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and shows cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is clear, original in its physiological chain of reasoning, and has exceptional patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, mechanism of action), Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action in humans) and Mojsov (peptide identification and early insulinotropic activity) form a plausible trio of three; Knudsen was decisive for drug development but is more translational, and the credited list may omit other early contributors such as Joel Habener, so I note this as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Therapeutic efficacy confirmed by many large independent trials and years of clinical use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue given current impact.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the early peptide discoverers (including people not on the credited list) is contested and I cannot verify it independently.
Whether the committee prefers to honour the physiology or the pharmaceutical development is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new modality of living drugs, with high originality as engineering of immune cells joined to tumor immunology.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain contributed decisive CAR designs and the clinical translation (costimulation, first successful trials); Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Others such as Zelig Eshhar and Gross are not in the credited list, so the allocation may be incomplete; I would weigh June and Sadelain most.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of clinical follow-up confirm efficacy in leukemia and lymphoma; solid tumors and toxicity remain unsolved, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Who should share with Rosenberg versus the original CAR concept inventors is uncertain.
Limited success in solid tumors and safety concerns may temper the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade controls disease turned a crippling condition into a manageable one and established cytokine-targeted therapy across inflammatory diseases. The concept chain from synovial cytokine biology to clinical proof is clear and of lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the bench-to-bedside program from cytokine cascade work to the first controlled anti-TNF trials; the pair is a natural and coherent two-person allocation. Contributions of the antibody engineers and other clinical groups are acknowledged but secondary to the concept.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation, several approved agents and broad use across diseases; recognition is timely to late.
uncertainties: Not on the credited list: the roles of other TNF discoverers and antibody developers may be argued by others.
As a rheumatology specialist I try to apply the same criteria as for other fields and rely on field-wide evidence rather than my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the thymus-dependent T-cell lineage and the bursa-dependent B-cell lineage was the foundation for modern adaptive immunology and for vaccines and immunotherapies; the discoveries are fundamental and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Miller identified the function of the thymus and T cells; Cooper (with Good and Peterson, not credited here) showed the B-cell lineage in the bursa and the two-lineage system. The credited pair gives a sound two-person configuration, though the absence of Robert Good, who is deceased, is notable.
assessment.maturity: Entirely confirmed over more than half a century; the matter is mature, and the main concern is whether the recognition is now very late and whether recent immunology prizes make it less urgent.
uncertainties: Age of the laureates and the possible unavailability of key historical contributors.
Overlap with earlier immunology prizes may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided splice-modulating antisense oligonucleotide therapy for SMN2 made a previously fatal infant neurodegenerative disease treatable; it validated antisense drugs and a general RNA-targeting therapeutic strategy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulation of SMN2 and the antisense target; Bennett led the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development with Ionis. These are the decisive two contributors, a clean allocation, though Adrian Krainer and the clinical development teams at Biogen add translational credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved drug with strong, long-term and independent clinical evidence; the platform effect on other antisense drugs is still developing, so timing is reasonable but the concept may be young.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this primarily as a drug-development success rather than a discovery of biology.
Durability of benefit across ages and later-onset treatment is still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger interferon and inflammatory responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus), cancer immunity and senescence. It is a clean, original mechanism with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger, which is the decisive step; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa co-discovered STING as well, and Wu and Sun were in Chen's lab, so the allocation of the STING part is arguably unsettled. Two names seem the best fit.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and extended across fields, with many therapeutic efforts underway, but clinical translation is not yet proven, so the prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competing claims on STING discovery between Barber and Ishikawa.
Therapeutic benefit has yet to be demonstrated in patients.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, transforming experimental biology; the channelrhodopsin discovery and its use as a tool are widely adopted. Medical impact is emerging but the methodological one is massive.
assessment.attribution: Six names are credited, so a trio must be chosen: Nagel and Hegemann identified channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth led the neuronal application and use in behavior. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck are also strong and the allocation is the most contested part.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used for 15 years; clinical use is still limited, though retinal optogenetic therapy has started. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Multiple strong claimants exceed the three-person limit.
Medical rather than tool-based impact is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 cloned at the t(14;18) translocation and shown to block cell death defined a new class of oncogene and the control of apoptosis, which led to BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax) in leukemias.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the molecular characterization of Bcl-2 family function and the mouse models; Vaux showed Bcl-2 acts by inhibiting cell death. Strasser is a major later contributor, and the initial cloning by Tsujimoto, Croce and others is not credited, so the primary claim of priority could be contested.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well confirmed and translated into an approved drug class, so it is mature; apoptosis already received the 2002 prize, which may reduce priority.
uncertainties: Priority issues with the original t(14;18) cloning groups outside this credited list.
Overlap with the earlier apoptosis prize.
